name: Wine shelf talker - Cave de Trevigne Coteaux Rouge

values.Buyer Note: The co-op red, and the wine I put in more hands than any other on the shelf. Carignan and grenache off old bush vines, unoaked, bottled young and honest. Bramble, black pepper and a little garrigue, soft enough to drink on a Tuesday but with real grip underneath. Fourteen pounds, and it drinks well above that so long as you open it a good hour before dinner.

name: Wine shelf talker - Domaine des Escaliers Cote Brune Syrah

values.Wine: Domaine des Escaliers Cote Brune Syrah
values.Buyer Note: A single-vineyard northern Rhone syrah off the steep brown schist above the river, co-fermented with a little viognier the way the hill has always done it. Black olive, cracked pepper, cured meat and violets, over a tannin still coiled tight. This wants five years in the cellar, or a decanter and a long lunch if you cannot wait that long.

name: Wine shelf talker - Cascina Voltone Nebbiolo

values.Buyer Note: A mature Piedmontese nebbiolo from a great vintage, ten years on and only now unwinding. Tar, dried rose, sour cherry and a dusting of woodsmoke over that famous grip of tannin and acid. Do not chill it and do not rush it: open it an hour ahead, pour it beside something with fat and salt, and let the middle of the bottle show you why we bought the allocation.

name: Wine shelf talker - Domaine Ravel Morgon

values.Buyer Note: The wine that changes how people think about Beaujolais. Cru gamay off granite, whole-bunch and unfiltered, so there is a savoury reduction on first pour that blows off into black cherry, iron and crushed violets. Serve it with a light chill against charcuterie or a roast chicken. If you still think gamay is thin and sweet, this is the bottle I would hand you to argue with.
